scams.location: Promenade des Anglais beach, Public beaches, Private beach clubs
scams.story: When tourists go swimming in the Mediterranean, thieves watch for unattended belongings on the beach. They quickly grab bags, wallets, phones, and cameras while the owner is distracted in the water. The thief disappears into the crowd before the victim returns to their towel.
red_flags: People loitering near beach areas watching swimmers
Someone positioning themselves near your belongings
Overly crowded beach sections
how_to_avoid: Never leave belongings unattended when swimming
Use your bag as a pillow when sunbathing
Bring a waterproof pouch to carry valuables while swimming
Travel with a companion who can watch your items

scams.location: Nice Airport, Train Station (Gare de Nice-Ville), Hotel pickups, Tourist areas
scams.story: Nice taxi drivers have a notorious reputation for overcharging tourists. Drivers may claim the meter is broken, quote inflated flat rates, obscure the meter with their hand to manipulate the fare, or take long routes. They often refuse credit cards and don't provide legally required receipts. Official fixed rates: Airport to Nice city center is €32, to Cannes is €85, to Monaco is €95.
red_flags: Driver says meter is broken
Driver quotes flat rate significantly above official prices
Driver's hand obscures the meter
Driver refuses credit card or receipt
how_to_avoid: Know official fixed rates before traveling
Always confirm the price before boarding
Insist on using the meter
Use Uber instead for transparent pricing
Always request a receipt

scams.location: Nice Côte d'Azur Airport, Airport tram terminals
scams.story: At Nice Airport, ticket machines only sell a special 'airport ticket' priced at €10 round trip. This is three times the actual cost of a regular tram ticket (€1.70). The machines are designed to extract maximum money from tourists who don't know about cheaper alternatives.
red_flags: Ticket machine at airport only showing expensive options
No visible regular fare options
how_to_avoid: Walk to Grand Arenas stop (one stop from airport) for regular ticket machines
Purchase tickets on the Lignes d'Azur mobile app
Be aware that regular fare is only €1.70

scams.location: Promenade des Anglais, Old Town (Vieux Nice), Near tourist attractions
scams.story: A stranger bends down near you and picks up what appears to be a gold ring, then asks if you dropped it. When you say no, they claim it's marked '14k gold' and must be valuable. They offer to sell it for a fraction of its 'worth' or demand a finder's fee. The ring is worthless brass. While engaging you, an accomplice may pickpocket you.
red_flags: Stranger conveniently 'finding' a ring right next to you
Ring appears suspiciously shiny
Persistent pressure to buy or give money
how_to_avoid: Simply say 'no' and walk away
Don't engage in conversation
Keep hands on your belongings
Be aware of accomplices nearby

scams.location: Promenade des Anglais, Old Town, Tourist attractions, Train station
scams.story: A young person approaches asking 'Speak English?' and presents a clipboard with a petition for a deaf charity. They use sign language to appear hearing-impaired. While you're distracted reading or signing, accomplices pickpocket you. If you sign, they demand a donation and become aggressive if refused.
red_flags: Young people with clipboards targeting tourists
Petition written in multiple languages
Person using exaggerated sign language
Multiple people hovering nearby
how_to_avoid: Firmly say 'no' and keep walking
Never sign anything on the street
Keep hands on your belongings when approached

scams.location: Busy streets, Near tourist attractions, Public squares
scams.story: One person secretly sprays liquid resembling bird droppings or mustard on your clothing from behind. Moments later, a 'helpful' stranger points out the mess and offers wet wipes to help clean you. While you're distracted removing your jacket or bag, accomplices steal your wallet, phone, or jewelry.
red_flags: Someone suddenly pointing out a stain you didn't notice
Overly helpful strangers offering to clean you
Multiple people surrounding you to 'help'
how_to_avoid: If you notice a stain, clean it yourself later
Never accept help from strangers for cleaning
Keep moving and find a safe private space
Hold onto your belongings tightly

scams.scam_name: Vol à la Portière (Car Door Grab)
scams.location: Traffic lights, Car parks, Parking garages, Rental car return areas
scams.story: Thieves target tourists in rental cars, identifiable by rental stickers or foreign plates. At traffic lights or in parking areas, they forcibly open the car door and snatch valuables from the seat. The crime happens in seconds, and the thieves disappear before victims can react.
red_flags: People on scooters or foot approaching stopped vehicles
Someone trying door handles at traffic lights
Loiterers in parking garages watching cars
how_to_avoid: Always lock car doors immediately upon entering
Keep windows rolled up, especially at traffic lights
Never leave valuables visible on seats
Consider removing rental company stickers

scams.location: Tourist attractions, Scenic viewpoints, Parking garages, Street parking
scams.story: Thieves stake out tourist sites, watching visitors park rental cars (easily identified by stickers and foreign plates). Knowing average visit times for each attraction, they break into cars and steal luggage, bags, and electronics while owners are sightseeing. France has one of the highest car break-in rates in Western Europe.
red_flags: People watching parking lots rather than visiting attractions
Broken glass on the ground near parking areas
how_to_avoid: Never leave any belongings visible in the car - even empty bags
Store everything in the trunk before arriving at your destination
Remove all tourist evidence (maps, guidebooks)
Use attended parking when available

scams.location: Tourist areas, Metro stations, Near bars at night
scams.story: Criminals pose as plainclothes police, quickly flashing fake badges. They demand to see your wallet for 'inspection' due to alleged counterfeit currency concerns. While examining your wallet, they steal cash. Sometimes a 'tourist' accomplice first asks you to break a large bill, then the fake officer arrives claiming street money exchange is illegal.
red_flags: Anyone stopping you to exchange money just before 'police' arrive
Plainclothes person claiming to be police
Quick flash of badge without allowing inspection
Request to see your wallet
how_to_avoid: Real police never ask to see your wallet - only ID documents
Ask to see official ID clearly
Insist on going to nearest police station
Never hand over your wallet to anyone on the street
Call 17 if suspicious

scams.location: Tourist restaurant areas, Promenade des Anglais restaurants, Old Town restaurants
scams.story: Tourist restaurants employ tactics to overcharge visitors. Waiters bring expensive bottled water instead of offering free tap water. Bills include items not ordered or charge premium prices shown only on the 'tourist menu.' Some waiters insist on automatic gratuity. Restaurants may refuse to let solo diners order less than a full multi-course meal.
red_flags: Waiter brings water without asking your preference
Different prices on French vs. English menus
Pressure to order multiple courses
Insistence on tip through card machine
how_to_avoid: Request 'une carafe d'eau' (tap water) - it's free by law
Ask for the French menu and compare prices
Check the bill carefully
Know that tipping is not obligatory in France

scams.story: Tourists buy tickets on Nice buses and trams but don't realize they must also validate (stamp) the ticket in a machine on board. Inspectors issue on-the-spot fines of €40 or more to tourists who have purchased tickets but failed to validate them. Bus drivers don't warn passengers about validation requirements.
red_flags: Yellow/orange validation machines on buses and trams
Other passengers inserting tickets into machines
how_to_avoid: Always validate your ticket immediately upon boarding
Listen for the 'beep' confirming validation
Watch what local passengers do
If unsure, ask the driver or another passenger

scams.location: Grand Arenas tram stop near airport
scams.story: Knowing that tourists go to Grand Arenas to avoid overpriced airport tickets, pickpockets (often teenage girls) target tired, luggage-laden visitors at ticket machines. One person offers to 'help' with the confusing ticket machine while an accomplice steals from your bag or pockets.
red_flags: Strangers offering unsolicited help at ticket machines
Multiple people gathering around you
Someone standing unusually close while you use the machine
how_to_avoid: Politely decline all offers of help
Keep bags in front of you and secured
Be aware of your surroundings
Have a travel companion watch your belongings

scams.location: Restaurant terraces, Promenade des Anglais, Romantic spots, Outdoor cafes
scams.story: Vendors approach couples at restaurants offering a 'free' rose. Once you accept or touch it, they aggressively demand 10-20 euros. They exploit social pressure, especially with couples where one partner may feel embarrassed to refuse. They become persistent and confrontational if payment is refused.
red_flags: Street vendor approaching with flowers at restaurants
Offering flowers as 'gifts'
Targeting couples specifically
how_to_avoid: Firmly say 'no' before touching anything
Put hands in pockets or cross arms
Don't feel guilty - this is a known scam
Ask restaurant staff to intervene if aggressive

scams.location: Standalone ATMs, Tourist area ATMs, ATMs in dimly lit areas
scams.story: Criminals attach hidden card readers (skimmers) and fake keypads to ATMs to capture card details and PINs. In some cases, a false slot insert causes the card to jam; when you leave to seek help, the scammer retrieves your card. Card data is then used for fraudulent transactions or clone cards.
red_flags: Card slot feels loose or bulky
Keypad feels thick or spongy
Any loose or unusual components
Card gets stuck in machine
Stranger offering help when card stuck
how_to_avoid: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours
Wiggle the card slot before inserting - skimmers are loosely attached
Cover keypad when entering PIN
If card gets stuck, do NOT leave - call bank immediately
Enable transaction alerts on your cards

scams.location: Promenade des Anglais, Luxury hotel areas, Nice city center
scams.story: The French Riviera has seen a surge in thefts of luxury watches. Thieves on scooters target tourists wearing expensive timepieces, pulling up alongside and forcibly removing watches. Some operate on foot, approaching in crowded areas to snatch watches off wrists. The attacks can be quick and violent.
red_flags: People on scooters watching pedestrians closely
Being followed while wearing expensive jewelry
Strangers commenting on your watch
how_to_avoid: Leave expensive watches at home or in hotel safe
If wearing a luxury watch, keep it covered with sleeves
Don't flash expensive jewelry in public
Consider travel insurance covering valuable items

scams.story: Scammers create fake listings on Airbnb, VRBO, or independent sites advertising attractive properties at below-market rates. After victims pay via wire transfer or outside the platform, they arrive to find the property doesn't exist, is occupied, or belongs to someone else. Some use stolen photos from legitimate listings.
red_flags: Price significantly below market rate
Host insists on communicating outside the platform
Payment requested via wire transfer
New host profile with no reviews
Urgency tactics
how_to_avoid: Book only through official platforms
Never pay outside the platform
Do reverse image searches on property photos
Read reviews carefully
Use credit card for payments (easier to dispute)
